problem: The chapter says a molecule absorbs a microwave photon 'only when ΔJ = ±1'. This states the quantum-number rule but never states the other necessary condition: the molecule must have a permanent electric dipole moment. A student can wrongly conclude that N₂ or O₂, which have no dipole moment, give a microwave rotational spectrum.
fix: Add: 'Two conditions are needed: the molecule must have a permanent dipole moment (so the rotating charge distribution can couple to the microwave field), and ΔJ = ±1. Homonuclear diatomics such as N₂ and O₂ have no permanent dipole moment and show no pure rotational spectrum.'

problem: 'The bond does not bend or stretch' is loose. A diatomic molecule has no bending motion at all; the only vibration it can have is stretching. Saying the bond does not bend can confuse students who later meet bending modes in polyatomics.
fix: Write: 'The bond length r is fixed; the bond does not stretch. (A diatomic has no bending mode; bending applies only to larger molecules.)'

problem: 'The gap between neighbouring levels grows with J, so successive absorption lines sit 2B apart' joins two facts with 'so', but the growing gap does not cause the equal spacing. A student may think the spacing grows too.
fix: Write: 'The gap between neighbouring levels grows steadily with J, from 2B between J = 0 and J = 1 to 2B(J+1) higher up. Because the gap grows linearly, every successive absorption line still sits exactly 2B away from the previous one.'
